Este es el tema central del bloque. Si s: This is the block's central topic. If you take only one idea away from here, let it be this one, because the next eight topics hang from it, along with a good part of the computer graphics of the last twenty years.
Este truco es la razón de que las letras: This trick is the reason letters read well on any screen. The fonts of video games and of many applications are stored not as images but as distance fields: a small texture where each pixel says how far it is from the letter's outline. On drawing it, a smoothstep reconstructs the perfect edge at any size, without pixelating. The technique was published by Chris Green, of Valve, in 2007, and today half the world uses it: it is why a game's title can be enlarged ten times and still have a clean edge.
Fíjate en que <strong>el campo existe en: Notice that the field exists over the whole screen, not only where the figure is. Every pixel in the universe knows how far it is from the circle. That extra information, which at first sight looks like a waste, is what makes it possible to do soft edges, shadows, outlines, unions of figures and, in [[gfx-raymarching|the raymarching topic]], whole three-dimensional geometry.
Fíjate en que en los extremos las dos co: Notice that at the extremes the two agree; the difference is in the middle, and that difference is the whole of the antialiasing.

La geometría por distancias se usaba en: Distance geometry had been used in simulation since the 1980s, but as an artists' tool it was popularised by the demoscene, that community which competes to fit whole animations into programs of 4 or 64 kilobytes. At that size neither models nor textures fit: everything has to fit in formulas. Out of it came techniques the industry later adopted. The production Elevated (2009), by Íñigo Quílez and Reinder Nijhoff, generates a mountain landscape with snow, water and fog in 4096 bytes, less than this paragraph repeated twenty times. Quílez later cofounded Shadertoy and published the distance formulas everybody uses today.
